title: Manchanabele at 5 AM
tagline: Two Ducatis, one windscreen. A pre-dawn run from Bengaluru along Magadi Road to a still reservoir with Savandurga on the horizon.
summary: A short, early-morning out-and-back from Bengaluru to the Manchanabele reservoir on the Arkavathy, on a Scrambler with a Desert X for company. Empty city roads at five, fast open stretches on Magadi Road, winding village tarmac and a red-earth track down to the water.

segments.note: Empty at five. Flyovers, then the city thins out and the road opens up for the fast bits.
Narrow, winding tarmac through villages, ending in a red-earth track down to the water.

highlights: Bengaluru at 5 AM with the roads to yourself
The open stretches of Magadi Road at first light
A flat-calm reservoir with Savandurga on the horizon
Mist on the far shore and reeds along the water's edge

offroad.summary: Tarmac all the way except the last red-earth track to the shore.
notes: The last stretch is packed earth with ruts and loose gravel, easy on any road bike ridden gently
Turns to paste when wet; park on firm ground, not the grassy edge
Road-biased dual-sport tyres (the Scrambler's Pirelli MT60 RS) are plenty

timings: Leave around 5 AM for empty roads and dawn light at the water
The dam area is listed as open 6 AM – 6 PM, entry free
Fuel up in the city; there's nothing you need to rely on near the reservoir
cautions: Do not enter the water: the reservoir bed has sudden drop-offs, boulders and deep slush, and many people have drowned here
Dawn is cold on a naked bike; layer up
Village stretch has livestock, speed breakers and early-morning foot traffic
No windscreen means wind blast on the fast sections; expect neck and shoulder fatigue

photos.caption: The Scrambler at the water's edge under the dawn sky
Red earth, still water, green hills
Barkbusters, mud and a red tank
